data.title: Results: Embecta Corp. Beat Earnings Expectations And Analysts Now Have New Forecasts
data.description:
As you might know, Embecta Corp. (NASDAQ:EMBC) just kicked off its latest annual results with some very strong numbers. The company beat forecasts, with revenue of US$1.1b, some 2.8% above estimates, and statutory earnings per share (EPS) coming in at US$2.15, 82% ahead of expectations. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their mind on Embecta after the latest results.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Embecta's four analysts is for revenues of US$1.08b in 2027. This reflects a reasonable 2.7% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are forecast to plunge 36% to US$1.49 in the same period. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of US$1.08b and earnings per share (EPS) of US$1.38 in 2027. The analysts seems to have become more bullish on the business, judging by their new earnings per share estimates.

View our latest analysis for Embecta

The average the analysts price target fell 50% to US$4.00, suggesting thatthe analysts have other concerns, and the improved earnings per share outlook was not enough to allay them. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. The most optimistic Embecta analyst has a price target of US$5.00 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$3.00. These price targets show that analysts do have some differing views on the business, but the estimates do not vary enough to suggest to us that some are betting on wild success or utter failure.

These estimates are interesting, but it can be useful to paint some more broad strokes when seeing how forecasts compare, both to the Embecta's past performance and to peers in the same industry. For example, we noticed that Embecta's rate of growth is expected to accelerate meaningfully, with revenues forecast to exhibit 2.7% growth to the end of 2027 on an annualised basis. That is well above its historical decline of 2.1% a year over the past five years. Compare this against analyst estimates for the broader industry, which suggest that (in aggregate) industry revenues are expected to grow 7.4% annually for the foreseeable future. Although Embecta's revenues are expected to improve, it seems that the analysts are still bearish on the business, forecasting it to grow slower than the broader industry.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing here is that the analysts upgraded their earnings per share estimates, suggesting that there has been a clear increase in optimism towards Embecta following these results. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. Furthermore, the analysts also cut their price targets, suggesting that the latest news has led to greater pessimism about the intrinsic value of the business.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. We have estimates - from multiple Embecta analysts - going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.

However, before you get too enthused, we've discovered 4 warning signs for Embecta (3 are a bit concerning!) that you should be aware of.

M&G has delivered a powerful 155.0% share price gain over the past 5 years, which puts a spotlight on what investors are really paying for today. The question now is whether the current valuation is properly anchored to the returns the business earns on its capital.

  • Over 5 years, M&G has returned 155.0%. This makes it important to ask if the underlying returns on capital are strong enough to support that kind of long run outcome.
  • The group’s model as an asset manager and savings provider means its valuation can hinge on how efficiently it reinvests client capital and its own balance sheet into projects that earn more than their funding cost.

Does M&G Look Undervalued on Excess Returns?

The Excess Returns model looks at how profit on equity compares to the cost of that equity. For M&G, the gap between the two is wide based on the inputs used here. Average Return on Equity sits at 23.95%, while the Cost of Equity is £0.12 per share against a Stable EPS estimate of £0.31 per share. That produces an Excess Return of £0.19 per share, which indicates the business is expected to earn more on its equity base than investors are assumed to require as compensation for risk.

Book Value is £1.09 per share and is projected to migrate toward a Stable Book Value of £1.29 per share, based on estimates from 6 analysts. On this framework, value is created when those above cost returns compound on a growing equity base, then compared with the current share price of £3.13. The Excess Returns projections put M&G's estimated intrinsic value substantially above the current share price, which is what the detailed output of this model is designed to show. data.title: Cloud Outage Might Change Microsoft (MSFT) Stock Narrative
data.description:
• Microsoft is contending with AI-heavy capital spending, a recent 24 hour global Microsoft 365 outage tied to a Windows scalability bug, and an internal Code Red effort to tighten reliability and incident response.
  • These pressures are pushing investors to focus less on headline AI wins and more on cash conversion, infrastructure payback, and operational resilience in Microsoft’s core cloud services.
  • We will look at how Microsoft’s long term investment case is affected by Code Red reliability fixes and AI driven capex pressure.

Scan how Microsoft’s Code Red reliability push and sovereign cloud deals compare with other large platforms by reviewing the hand picked 52 AI infrastructure stocks shaping the next phase of AI data center buildouts.

Microsoft Investment Narrative Recap

To own Microsoft here, you need to believe heavy AI and data center capex eventually translates into durable cloud, productivity and agentic AI cash flows, not just headline product launches. According to CubanEros, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the key watchpoint is whether this spend, now funded from operating strength, keeps earning high returns without straining the balance sheet.

In the short term, the main catalyst is execution on AI infrastructure while keeping Microsoft 365 and Azure reliable after the Code Red outage. The biggest risk is ongoing reliability or security incidents that undermine that trust and delay payback on AI spend. Recent announcements do not materially change that risk reward balance.

The extended sovereignty partnership with Atos matters most right now because it sits exactly where investors are focused: AI heavy spend, cash conversion, and whether Microsoft can win long duration workloads that fit strict European sovereignty rules. These projects test whether today’s data center outlay supports higher value, highly regulated cloud and AI demand.

For your checklist, Atos’ “sovereignty by design” work atop Microsoft’s EU Data Boundary shows how Code Red reliability goals, security controls and AI services need to mesh in practice. Execution risk is real because complex sovereign environments raise operational demands and cost. If Microsoft runs these securely and efficiently, they support the current capex cycle rather than extend it.

CubanEros estimates a fair value of US$419.91 for Microsoft using a discounted cash flow style framework that combines 10.2% annual revenue growth with a future profit margin of 39.3%, stating that this mix supports a premium multiple on what they view as resilient cash generation.

Uncover why Microsoft's fair value indicates a 14% potential downside to its current price, which could expose a premium that may not hold.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One alternate view puts Code Red reliability worries in the shadow of Microsoft’s heavy AI capex. The lowest analysts were already braced for profit margins to narrow from 41.2% to 33.6%, even while forecasting revenue around US$555.6b and earnings near US$186.7b by 2029. That is a much more cautious story on AI returns.
